articles.title: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ Players Are Losing Loot to Server Crashes Despite Official Fix from Infinity Ward
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's new extraction mode, DMZ, is experiencing server issues, causing players to lose newly earned loot.
articles.body:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's new extraction mode, DMZ, is experiencing server issues, causing players to lose newly earned loot.

Yesterday, Infinity Ward put its new extraction mode into early access ahead of MW4's full release on Friday. It's giving players a chance to mess around with the game's other offerings before the main course is unleashed, and while the reception has been glowing so far, there are some issues. The game's been having server crashes, casuing to players lose any loot they picked up.

Thankfully, any loot that you already extracted to the FOB and brought back into the DMZ as part of a loadout is safe, but anything you picked up during the run that you were booted from is lost. Infinity Ward claims the matter has been fixed and has confirmed what players will keep and lose.

All Guns and Weapons in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4

"Players who disconnected due to this particular issue will retain the equipment they started the match with and their subsequent progression, but not the loot collected during the match," devs said in an update on Twitter/X.

📢 Call of Duty: #ModernWarfare4 | #DMZ Early Access We’re aware of an issue causing some players to disconnect from matches. We’ve deployed a potential fix and are monitoring the results. Players who disconnected due to this particular issue will retain the equipment they started the match with and their subsequent progression, but not the loot collected during the match. — Call of Duty Updates (@CODUpdates) October 21, 2026

📢 Call of Duty: #ModernWarfare4 | #DMZ Early Access We’re aware of an issue causing some players to disconnect from matches. We’ve deployed a potential fix and are monitoring the results. Players who disconnected due to this particular issue will retain the equipment they started the match with and their subsequent progression, but not the loot collected during the match.

Some players are still reporting problems, so your mileage may vary. Of course, it's difficult to ensure everything that a player had when they were booted is safe. If that were the case, it could theoretically be abused by players to extract valuable loot without having to actually find an extraction zone. Still, if you found something extremely rare or valuable and lost it due to technical issues, it would be extremely frustrating.

Black Ops 7's Endgame mode had similar issues when it launched last year. The PvE extraction mode encouraged players to grind for rewards, but if you died or failed to extract, you would lose everything. Unfortunately, that also applied to crashes during the game's first few days. This was eventually fixed, but it was an agonizing first impression for anyone who spent hours grinding the game, only for it to be undone by something out of your control.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's full release will hit on October 23. The game's acclaimed campaign and DMZ modes are available to play now for owners of the title.

articles.title: The Long Game: The Best Upgrades for Each Vehicle in Star Wars: Galactic Racer
articles.body:
We’re back for another entry in our The Long Game series, where we go over things you can invest in early in games that pay off in the long run. This time, we’re traveling to a galaxy far, far away for Star Wars: Galactic Racer, the new racing game from Fuse Games.

First, we should start with the basics. Galactic Racer gives you three vehicles to choose from, and they come with very different strengths and weaknesses. You can upgrade all three, but it pays to understand which stats are important for each vehicle, especially to prepare you for the more difficult challenges that await later in the game.

There are both temporary and permanent upgrades, and throughout the single-player campaign, you’ll get a random set of three to choose from. Certain multiplayer modes also let you choose from random sets of temporary upgrades, but permanent ones are exclusive to the campaign.

Upgrades cost tuning points, which are basically Galactic Racer’s version of skill points, and the cost goes up each time you upgrade. You can respec your allocated points, so you won’t get stuck with an unoptimized vehicle, but these are the upgrades we recommend focusing on for each vehicle.

The Landspeeder is your standard, well-balanced vehicle. It has easy handling and high defense against collisions, whether you’re hitting the walls of the track or being attacked by your fellow racers. Since it’s naturally balanced, we recommend you focus on upgrades that allow for a little more creativity during races.

That starts with upgrading the Afterburner, which affects your acceleration, deceleration, and boost power. It allows you to boost more frequently and hit a higher top speed, and the benefit of being able to go faster in a race should be pretty obvious. We also recommend upgrading the Ramjet for basically the same reason, it’ll get you higher top speeds.

Lastly, it’s a good idea to upgrade the Battery, which determines how often you’re able to activate your abilities. Since the Landspeeder has such balanced stats, it lends itself to a wide variety of different abilities.

The Speeder Bike is the smallest of the vehicles, but it also has the fastest acceleration and a special Kinetic Burst that gives you an extra boost when you come out of a drift. We recommend leaning into that and creating your build around it.

Upgrading Kinetic Burst improves both the speed you maintain during a drift and your boost when finishing it. However, to handle that increased speed, you also need to upgrade your Cornering. It gives you better handling around tight turns, allowing you to harness your excellent drifting speed without careening into the wall.

While the Speeder Bike is quick, it’s also fragile and a common target for your opponents. To combat that, we recommend upgrading its Resilience, which is basically its defense. It’s never going to be a tank, but making it at least a bit sturdier can help with its main weakness.

Last but not least, the Skim Speeder is the widest of the bunch, and we recommend using that to your advantage. Its sturdier body makes it the best option for going on the offensive and attacking opposing racers.

Upgrading your Ramjet allows you to turn your vehicle into a missile that can clip other vehicles without endangering your own pilot. Of course, since you’re going to be taking a lot of contact with this playstyle, you should also upgrade your Resilience.

The main weakness of the Skim Speeder is also thanks to its width: it’s harder to handle, especially around turns. To help address that issue, we recommend upgrading your Cornering. Basically, with the Skim Speeder and Bike Speeder, you should upgrade both Cornering and Resilience, but for opposite reasons because their strengths are also opposites.

articles.title: BioWare Shutting Down, Next Mass Effect Canceled
articles.summary: BioWare is shutting down and the next Mass Effect game is canceled, according to a new report.
articles.body:
BioWare is shutting down and the next Mass Effect game is canceled, EA has announced.

Bloomberg said BioWare closes its doors amid mass layoffs at Electronic Arts, which amount to 400 people losing their jobs (approx. 3% of total staff). Roughly 50 of these roles were at BioWare.

After the franchise-best sales of Dragon Age: Inquisition, BioWare sought live-service success with Anthem, then spent the best part of a decade on the troubled Dragon Age: The Veilguard. Both underperformed. Mass Effect, meanwhile, has seen mixed success. Mass Effect Andromeda is widely considered a disappointment among fans, though the series' more recent Legendary Edition remaster was well-received.

BioWare had spent the past half a decade gradual teasing the next Mass Effect's setting and story. We'd had it confirmed that Mass Effect 5 would have been set hundreds of years after Mass Effect 3 , and feature a narrative that re-centers the action on the franchise's original Milky Way setting, long after the Reapers were defeated. Now, fans will never find out what happens next.

It is unclear what this means for Amazon's live-action Mass Effect series, which was also meant to be set after the events of Mass Effect 3 and tell a fresh story. Earlier this year, Mass Effect TV series co-showrunner Daniel Casey refuted a report that suggested the upcoming adaptation had recently undergone rewrites to be "more appealing to non-gamers."

EA will continue with sports games, Respawn's Apex Legends, action-adventure games (Star Wars: Jedi 3 and Marvel's Iron Man), and Battlefield. Bloomberg said Respawn and DICE are likely working on Star Wars: Battlefront 3, as had been rumored.

The drastic cuts come just a few months after EA went private in a leveraged buyout worth $55 billion, backed in large part by the Saudi Public Investment Fund, as well as the U.S. private equity firm Silver lake and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners.

In a memo sent to staff today, Cam Weber, president and chief studios officer, and David Tinson, president and COO, described itself as "the number one publisher in Western HD gaming, but "our industry is changing quickly."

"Players have more choices than ever for their time and attention, competition is intensifying, and some of our biggest opportunities for growth are beyond the markets, platforms, and business models where EA has traditionally been the strongest," they said.

EA reacted to this by "concentrating our teams, technology, and investment" behind three strategic priorities: "Deepen Our Core; "Expand Our Reach;" and "Transform Our Business."

"Our greatest opportunity starts with our franchises and global communities that have made EA a leader in interactive entertainment," the pair continued. "This is where we’ve had to make our hardest choices. Saying no to some things we're passionate about allows us to focus our teams and resources so we give our biggest opportunities everything they need to succeed."

Last year's Battlefield 6 was a "great success." Future Battlefield games are on the way, as well as the Respawn and DICE collaboration project that is believed to be Star Wars: Battlefront 3. EA said it will also continue to "invest heavily" in Respawn's battle royale, Apex Legends, over the next few years by introducing brand new gameplay modes in multiplayer, and "other new experiences, to expand the universe."

Marvel’s Iron Man (EA Motive) and the next Star Wars Jedi 3 (Respawn) live on, but expect "fewer simultaneous, large-scale projects," in the action-adventure genre from EA. And here's the official blurb on the end of BioWare and Mass Effect:

As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly.

EA Sports will of course continue the FC franchise. Two new projects are in development which are due to be revealed in the next few months: "a brand-new, social-first open-world experience for our American Football team that we call 'Project Gridiron,' and we are also in pre-production to bring back a beloved, fan-favorite in Fight Night, leveraging capabilities from our simulation fighting team."

The "Lifestyle," category, as EA calls it, will see Project Evergreen continue but Project Lotus paused. Both are The Sims projects. Skate, meanwhile, had "a lot of success in bringing players into the game, and we need to create an experience that keeps them engaged over the long-term. To do that, we are making changes to the studio to have a more focused, smaller team to deliver on a very clear roadmap for our community that we believe will build a healthier and more sustainable business."

Less than 12 months ago, Mike Gamble, executive producer of Mass Effect at BioWare, celebrated N7 Day to say the next Mass Effect game was still in development, to express excitement about the Amazon TV series, and to insist EA and BioWare "remain committed to telling more stories in this universe."

In a social media post published today, Gamble told fans, "Your support has meant everything to me over the past 17 years at BioWare."

articles.title: Anime Characters Dominate Top Trending Pet Names of 2026
articles.summary: The top-trending dog and cat names in the United States are dominated by anime characters from franchises such as KPop Demon Hunters and Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle.
articles.body:
The top-trending dog and cat names in the United States are dominated by anime characters from franchises such as KPop Demon Hunters and Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle . Characters from The Odyssey and Star Wars: Andor also made the cut.

Names derived from movies and TV shows were the third highest trend in US pet names behind the categories of cottagecore and vintage revival, according to Rover .

The site reveals the top two trending dog names of 2026 are Rumi (KPop Demon Hunters) and Lumi (Lumi and the Great Big Galaxy).

Among dogs, Rover’s top trending movie/TV pet names are Telemachus (The Odyssey), Kleya (Andor), Heathcliff (Wuthering Heights), Fiyero (Wicked: For Good) and Jinu (KPop Demon Hunters).

The Top 25 Greatest Anime Characters of All Time

The top five trending names for cats are Giyu (Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle), Shinobu (Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle), Jinu (KPop Demon Hunters), Derpy (KPop Demon Hunters), and Nessa (Wicked: For Good).

“New names inspired by the big screen this year include Dek (from Predator: Badlands), Reze (from Chainsaw Man: Reze Arc) and Slurp (from Wednesday) for dogs. New for cats are Kamek (from The Super Mario Bros. Movie), Kleya (from Andor) and Makima (from Chainsaw Man: Reze Arc),” according to Rover.

What’s your pet’s name? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: EA is shutting down BioWare
articles.summary: Amid 400 job cuts, Electronic Arts is shutting down BioWare, the storied studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic.
articles.body: BioWare, the legendary studio behind RPGs like Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, is shutting down, the company confirmed in a statement. Alongside the closure, Electronic Arts has chosen not to continue development on the next Mass Effect game that was in the works, according to an announcement sent to EA staff. The company is also laying off around 400 staffers, Bloomberg reports, including around 50 at BioWare. The changes follow EA being taken private by an investor group led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners in a $55 billion deal that closed in August. Other major gaming companies have made sweeping changes this year as well, including Xbox’s “reset” that will include 3,200 cuts, Bungie’s “significant” layoffs, and Fortnite maker Epic Games laying off over 1,000 staff. “BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” Cam Weber, EA president and chief studios officer, and David Tinson, EA president and COO, said in the announcement. Here is the full message that BioWare shared on social media: > For more than 30 years, BioWare has been more than a studio. It has been a home for storytellers, developers, and the players who brought our worlds to life. > Baldur’s Gate. Neverwinter Nights. Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic. Dragon Age. Mass Effect. Anthem. > Now, after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending. > There is nothing easy about writing those words. Our focus right now is on our incredibly talented team who put their hearts into these games, and supporting one another through this transition. > What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember. These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own. > From all of us at BioWare, thank you for being the most meaningful part of our story. While the end of BioWare will shock many gamers who fondly remember its hits, the company hasn’t been as successful in recent years. 2017’s Mass Effect: Andromeda was widely seen as a misstep for that franchise, it took a big bet on live service games in 2019 with Anthem that didn’t pan out, and EA laid off some BioWare staff in 2025 after Dragon Age: The Veilguard missed sales expectations. There is no word yet on the fate of Amazon’s Mass Effect TV series. Last we heard, Amazon’s head of TV was close to giving it the green light, but had reportedly requested rewrites to make the show “more appealing to non-gamers.” Amazon didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. EA spokesperson Justin Higgs said he had “Nothing to share on that at this point.” In EA’s company-wide announcement, Weber and Tinson outlined several other projects in development and changes to EA’s roadmap. The executives say that Respawn and DICE will be collaborating on “a future project,” which Bloomberg says is “likely” a new Star Wars: Battlefront game. The company is still working Marvel’s Iron Man and a new Star Wars Jedi title. EA is making a “brand-new, social-first open-world experience” football game that it calls “Project Gridiron” and is also in pre-production on a new Fight Night boxing title (which was teased yesterday). For The Sims, the company is pausing development on “Project Lotus” and focusing on “Project Evergreen.” And for its live-service Skate, EA is “making changes to the studio” to “deliver on a very clear roadmap for our community.” Here is the full message from Weber and Tinson at Electronic Arts: > Hi Team, > First, thank you. > Through every major moment we’ve faced as a company, your commitment to creating awesome games and experiences for our players continues to be impressive. Together, we’ve built epic worlds and global communities that are part of the lives of hundreds of millions of people. > Today, we’re the number one publisher in Western HD gaming. That’s an extraordinary position to lead from, and one we should be proud of. Yet our industry is changing quickly. Players have more choices than ever for their time and attention, competition is intensifying, and some of our biggest opportunities for growth are beyond the markets, platforms, and business models where EA has traditionally been the strongest. > That’s why, over the past several months, we’ve taken a hard look at our business, how we operate, and what it will take to lead in this next era of interactive entertainment. We’ve challenged assumptions, confronted hard realities, imagined new possibilities, and made deliberate choices in order to deliver exceptional experiences for our players and to drive sustained growth. > We believe our best creative work happens when we’re clear about what matters most for our players and give our teams the freedom to move quickly. So, we’re concentrating our teams, technology, and investment behind these three strategic priorities. > * Deepen Our Core: Our greatest opportunity starts with our franchises and global communities that have made EA a leader in interactive entertainment. This is where we’ve had to make our hardest choices. Saying no to some things we’re passionate about allows us to focus our teams and resources so we give our biggest opportunities everything they need to succeed. * Expand Our Reach: The strength of our core business creates an enormous opportunity to reach more players across new platforms, markets, and business models. As one example, in regions as dynamic as Asia, success means building experiences that reflect local players, cultures, and expectations. * Transform Our Business: We believe we can use our experience building interactive entertainment, together with our relationships in sports, to create entirely new ways for fans to engage with the teams, athletes and sports they love. These will be disciplined investments that only scale when they demonstrate real potential. > These priorities will bring clarity and focus to your work every day, and so will the way we work. We’ve spent time listening to teams about what’s working, what’s getting in the way, and what you need to do your best work. The feedback was consistent: you want clearer priorities, faster decisions, and teams that work more closely together. We’ve already begun simplifying how we work so we can spend more time creating and innovating for our players. > Our Portfolio Choices > Across our portfolio, we’re making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth. > In our Shooters business, Battlefield 6 was a great success, and we learned a lot from the launch and the live service. We’re going to take those learnings, balance our resources, and leverage the technology to deliver a shooter portfolio that unlocks growth. In addition to our future Battlefield titles, we’ll be bringing together our Respawn and DICE studios to collaborate on a future project that will help us achieve that ambition. We can’t wait to share more when the time comes. We’re also continuing to invest heavily in Apex over the next few years by introducing brand new gameplay modes in multiplayer, and other new experiences, to expand the universe. > Action-adventure is one of the most competitive and high-stakes genres in the industry, where every game needs our full weight behind it. We’re continuing to deliver on our two huge launches coming up with Marvel’s Iron Man and the next Star Wars Jedi game. Beyond that, we will concentrate our efforts on fewer simultaneous, large-scale projects, ensuring that every game we build in this space is fully set up for success. > As we focus on these larger opportunities, we’ve had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We’ve made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly. > EA SPORTS continues to operate from a position of strength. We are fully committed and investing in the global growth of our FC franchise and across the full EA SPORTS portfolio. We have two new projects in development you’ll hear about over the next few months, including a brand-new, social-first open-world experience for our American Football team that we call “Project Gridiron,” and we are also in pre-production to bring back a beloved, fan-favorite in Fight Night, leveraging capabilities from our simulation fighting team. > In Lifestyle, we’re focusing on the long-term potential of The Sims and skate. We’re going to prioritize our efforts on “Project Evergreen” for The Sims to give the team more time to reach the full potential and vision for the game, and to help make this possible, we’re pausing development on “Project Lotus.” For skate., we’ve had a lot of success in bringing players into the game, and we need to create an experience that keeps them engaged over the long-term. To do that, we are making changes to the studio to have a more focused, smaller team to deliver on a very clear roadmap for our community that we believe will build a healthier and more sustainable business. > Building the EA We Believe In > The decisions we’re making in our priorities, how we work, and with our portfolio reflect our belief in EA’s future. Some open exciting new possibilities. Others are difficult, especially for the people and teams across the company who are directly affected. In those cases, we will support impacted employees in exploring other opportunities within EA, and we’re committed to treating impacted colleagues with care and respect. > We’re sure there will be questions about what these changes mean for individual teams and for EA more broadly. You can speak directly with your leaders to hear more on that, and we’ll make sure to spend time discussing our direction and the work ahead at our next Global Town Hall in November. > The past several months have strengthened our belief in what EA can become. We have extraordinary people, franchises that matter to millions of players, and opportunities to build experiences we’ve only begun to imagine. > Our responsibility is to make the choices, provide the clarity, and create the conditions for our teams to do their best work. We also want to give every game we choose to build its best chance to succeed for our players and fans around the world. > We look forward to building more great games and experiences together. > Thanks, > Cam & David

articles.title: This Massive 70" 4K Fire TV Drops to a Mere $299.99 With Free Delivery Ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary: Lowest priced 70" TV for 2026.
articles.body:
Ahead of Black Friday, Best Buy is offering the lowest price I've seen this year for a massive (70" or higher) TV. For this week only, you can pick up the 70" Insignia F50 4K Fire TV for just $299.99 with free shipping. It's sold and shipped by Best Buy direct, not a marketplace vendor, and comes with a 1 year warranty.

Early Black Friday Deal: 70" Insignia 4K Fire TV for Just $300

As far as TVs are concerned, my rule of thumb is bigger is better as long as you have enough space. If you're on a budget and want the best bang for your buck, screen size will nearly always make a bigger impression than any other feature. The Insignia F50 is a void-filling 70" TV featuring a native 4K 60Hz display with HDR10 and HLG support and built-in Fire TV.

This is a solid TV for PlayStation 5 gaming despite the fact that it doesn't have a native 120Hz refresh rate. Unless you're rocking a PS5 Pro , the vast majority of games can't push past 60fps. Playing Grand Theft Auto 6 on a 70" TV, for example, will be a much more profound real-world experience than playing it on a 120Hz TV. Likewise, the Insignia F50 is a great TV for Nintendo Switch gamers because the Switch 2 only supports 60Hz at 4K in docked mode .

For the amount you save compared to getting a higher end TV, you could buy yourself a ton of video games and maybe even another console. For many (probably most) people, that's money better spent.

articles.title: Slow Horses Season 6 Finale Review: A Decent Season Wrap-Up That's Overshadowed by the Episode's Mysterious Cliffhanger
articles.summary: The Slow Horses need to wiggle out of a dire situation in a season finale once more. Of course, they do — but not without casualties. Season 6 ends by tying up all of its loose ends; it just takes a couple of leaps and conventional storytelling moves, at least for Slow Horses, to get there. Add in the massive cliffhanger, and you’ve got a decent finale that sets the stage for Season 7 next year.
articles.body:
This review contains full spoilers for Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 6, which is streaming on Apple TV now.

The Slow Horses always find themselves in dire situations in season finales. To that end, the closer of Season 6 is no different. They’re chased and hunted and shot at again and again. They scheme (well, Gary Oldman’s Jackson Lamb does) to save their behinds — remember, Moscow rules. Reece Nesmith (Lenny Rush) gets his hero moment, pulling off a Chekov’s harpoon. In a moment of stillness, River Cartwright (Jack Lowden) has it out with his dear old dad, Frank Harkness (Hugo Weaving), who might have a soft spot for his son after all. The mess with the Russians closes with Clayface Jane (MyAnna Buring) dead and MI5 handing over a fall guy that isn’t Sid Baker (Olivia Cooke, who shamefully only gets three seconds of distant screentime this episode).

And yet, even with the endless game of survival the agents play against their agitators, this finale doesn’t feel particularly novel for a series that has given us 11th-hour twists and feel-bad yet satisfying endings for its five prior seasons. Yes, it closed on a huge cliffhanger that sets Slow Horses up for Season 7 (due out next year — get those theories cranking about what, exactly, took River down), but it was all just a little too clean and conventional in a show that has typically embraced the mess.

To neatly tie up all of the loose ends, the show had to make a few leaps. The most egregious is Diana Taverner (Kristin Scott Thomas, who nevertheless has given a fantastic performance all season). It’s a bit of a stretch to believe that Diana, after an entire season of quadrupling down on denials and obfuscation, would finally decide to come clean and admit to treason, and even more of a stretch to think that Jackson Lamb (Gary Oldman) would be the one to convince her how to play it. It was hardly surprising, although nonetheless satisfying, that Damien Cantor and Peter Judd were made to be patsies for the Russians essentially financing a hit on their own soil, but it was somewhat curious at how easily the Home Secretary accepted Diana’s finger pointing as fact. It still seems Diana will face some consequences, based on the teaser for next season which seems to be Shirley (woohoo!) and Ho-centric, but one would think an accusation of treason would come with a heftier investigation rather than just taking the First Desk at her word.

Cantor (Harry Lloyd), in retrospect, was a somewhat disappointing bad guy. In the end, he only mattered in the context of giving the main characters a headache for a couple days. He never showed off his media influence, aside from one viral interview and that he could eat dinners in fancy restaurants alone. We never get a sense of how his news outlet operated in society, though there were plenty of inferences to be made, of course, but Slow Horses has never shied away from being explicit with an antagonist’s ugliness. Even just last season, Ho’s honey trap and her Libyan terrorist group, seeking revenge for Britain’s heavy hand in their country’s destabilization, had far richer characterization. Here, Cantor was a fairly one-note villain-of-the-season (he barely even speaks during his first appearance in Episode 1), motivated by winning a Russian media distribution contract that was mentioned in a single scene.

Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 6 — Images

Pivoting to the rigamarole of Slough House, their chilling at the posh safehouse by Harkness and his goons. Their flee-and-hide routine in the final showdown in Diana’s holiday home and along the lakeshores has its share of exciting moments. (Also, how the hell did River find his way there?) Having them break off into teams was functionally necessary for these scenes, but the compartmentalization often impacted the momentum of things and came off like a stop-and-start game of fight tactics. No offense, but I don’t want Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave in my TV show, thanks. But RIP Emma Flyte (Ruth Bradley), gone too soon but sticking by her word to be the group’s distraction. Louisa Guy (Rosalind Eleazar) also had a scary brush with mortality, but it also wasn’t hugely surprising to see her alive by the end; it would have been too much to kill her off, even for Slow Horses.

The most interesting revelation from that sequence was the curtain-pull on Harkness’s motivations. From that came an actual moment of uncertainty: if he would still go and kill Reece after Cantor called him off. He holds himself to the terms of the job after all. Harkness might have explained away killing Jane as an act of stopping the dangerous pursuer, but it certainly felt bigger than that as he offered River a drink in the aftermath of it all. River letting him get away bookends that short interaction in a meaningful way (and now the show can still deploy Harkness in future seasons).

The last scene back at River’s grandad’s house — where, in a sweet gesture, Sid kept her promise from the last episode, leaving a light on for River — was almost a lovely moment for an agent who’s had a terrible last few days. That final scene of River going for tea, then wine, then collapsing raises a ton of questions, of course. There’s the paranoia around Sid: Did she lure him there? Is she bad after all? More likely, I think, Jim and Jane planted something on one of the objects he touched, knowing that he would return to the house and getting their job done from beyond the grave. Jim did grab the crowbar in Episode 3 when they first broke into the house, and River made a whole show of the residue when he grabbed it. But that seems too obvious. Even though Season 6 laid its tracks maybe too bare, I’m still prepared to be made a fool by Slow Horses again.

articles.summary: This 0.7" thin power bank boasts high capacity and output for handheld gaming PCs and laptops.
articles.body:
Looking for a high-capacity, high-output power bank with an ultra-slim footprint? Ahead of Black Friday, Amazon has dropped the price of the Baseus Blade 20,000mAh 100W power bank to just $39.49 shipped after you apply coupon code " Z6J1ANOV ". You do NOT have to be an Amazon Prime member. Unlike most high-capacity power banks that are shaped like a chunky bar, the Baseus Blade is slimmer. It's powerful enough to charge any gaming handheld PC at its fastest rate. This is consistently one of the most popular power banks on IGN whenever I post a deal for it (which isn't often).

Baseus Blade 20,000mAh 100W Slim Power Bank for $39.49

Baseus Blade 20,000mAh 100W Slim Power Bank

The Baseus Blade measures only 0.7 inches thick. Most high-capacity power banks are well over 1" in thickness. The Blade achieves this slim depth by going with a wider body design. articles.title: EA Confirms DICE and Respawn Are Collaborating on a New Project Amidst Star Wars: Battlefront 3 Rumors
articles.summary: EA has confirmed that DICE and Respawn are working on a new project together, adding more fuel to rumors about Star Wars: Battlefront 3.
articles.body:
EA has confirmed that DICE and Respawn are working on a new project together, adding more fuel to rumors about Star Wars: Battlefront 3 .

As part of a larger letter about the future of EA, the publisher confirmed that it is working on new Battlefield games. It also noted that in addition to Battlefield, DICE and Respawn are working together on a "future project" that they hope will unlock growth in their shooter portfolio. This follows rumors from earlier this week that the two companies are working together to make Star Wars: Battlefront 3.

"In addition to our future Battlefield titles, we’ll be bringing together our Respawn and DICE studios to collaborate on a future project that will help us achieve that ambition," said EA. "We can’t wait to share more when the time comes."

Every Planet and Location in Star Wars Battlefront 2's Multiplayer

Variety also corroborated the Battlefront 3 rumors via sources, though nothing was shared on what the game will look like or when it might release. Other rumors recently suggested that Bungie was in the mix to work on Battlefront 3 or perhaps another project in the Star Wars universe, though nothing has been confirmed on that front. Star Wars: Battlefront 3 has been one of the most demanded titles over the last decade.

DICE's second crack at the Star Wars shooter franchise was controversial at launch due to issues with its monetization strategy , but the game itself was praised up and down by fans. It has remained a respected title among Star Wars lovers, and they've frequently rallied together to demand a sequel . Now, it seems like it will happen, though this time with the assistance of Respawn.

The Titanfall and Apex Legends studio has its own experience working on Star Wars through the Jedi games and the recently-released Star Wars Zero Company. Respawn also worked on a canceled Star Wars shooter, rumored to be a Mandalorian game, leaving fans to wonder what could've been. Only time will tell what this new Respawn and DICE game really is, but if it's Battlefront 3, it has serious potential to be something special.

This news came alongside some doom and gloom. EA confirmed that it was canceling the next Mass Effect and shutting down veteran RPG studio BioWare . The news comes after about a decade of commercial and critical misfires from the studio with games like Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard.

articles.title: We Build LEGO Hubble Space Telescope: a Miniature Homage to Cosmic Discovery
articles.body:
Ever since I was a child, I've always been fascinated by space. I would look up at the night sky and dream of one day becoming an astronaut, endlessly exploring the cosmos. Then I got older and decided that being stuck in a small spacecraft for months on end probably wasn't a great idea (thanks, anxiety). But my love for space still lives on, and when I saw that LEGO announced a replica of the Hubble Space Telescope, I knew I had to have it.

LEGO partnered with NASA and the European Space Agency (ESA), the two agencies responsible for building the Hubble Space Telescope, to create an accurate replica commemorating the 35th anniversary of its launch. You can purchase the LEGO Hubble Space Telescope now from Amazon and the LEGO Store .

LEGO is no stranger to making space-themed sets , with plenty of other NASA replicas available including the massive Artemis Space Launch System and the Mars Rover Perseverence, as well as sets based on popular space franchises like Star Trek and the recent Project Hail Mary . But, what I really want is for LEGO to bring back some of the classic 90's space sets like Exploriens and Spyrius – those were the best.

LEGO Hubble Space Telescope is built in three major sections spread across nine bags: the stand, the back portion that houses the instrument bay, and the narrower shaft on the front. This was a very relaxing set to put together, and pairs rather nicely with a space-themed synthwave playlist.

You begin by putting together the stand on which Hubble will be displayed. Unlike most LEGO stands, this one uses some interesting techniques with interlocking Technics pieces to create an angled post that allows the Hubble to "dock" when it's on display, helping to stabilize the unit.

At the base of the display are three translucent printed pieces depicting some of Hubble's most iconic Deep Field images: Pillars of Creation, the Whirlpool Galaxy, and the Butterfly Nebula. These are some of the coolest unique pieces I've seen LEGO make, and they look great integrated into the stand. It also includes a small plaque (which is unfortunately a large sticker on a flat piece) on the side of the support arm that provides information about Hubble, including its overall dimensions, weight, launch date, and the dates of key service missions.

While building this set, I actually learned quite a bit about the Hubble and its inner workings. Over the last three decades, it has recorded more than 1.7 million observations of our universe, producing some absolutely stunning imagery , as it circles in low-earth orbit. The instruction manual includes quite a few interesting facts about the Hubble Telescope, as well as a diagram of all of the scientific instruments recreated inside this LEGO model.

After finishing the stand, you move onto what is arguably the most important section of the Hubble: its large bottom half that houses many of its critical systems and instruments. While I expected this portion to be interesting to put together, it was fairly repetitive, as it's a lot of symmetrical sections and repeated instructions.

It didn't help that much of what I was putting together wasn't recognizable. If it weren't for the diagram in the instruction manual, I would have no concept of what I was building until the outer panels were attached. After all, most of the important components of the advanced camera and spectographs are represented by just four brown corner wall panel pieces.

Because each side is nearly identical, it's easy to get the orientaton mixed up if you're not careful. I think this is why LEGO added (what seemed to be) a random green piece on only one of the sides to help ensure you don't misplace any pieces.

After building the interior and some of the instruments, you add the panels to three of the four sides. The final side is intended to be removable, so you can look inside the bottom section and see the camera, mirrors, sensors, and baffle.

Building Hubble's upper shaft is mostly just putting together four long outer panels. Like the bottom half, the outer paneling is mostly rounded grey pieces and can get quite repetitive. These panels are all long and not very thick, so attaching them to the rest of the build requires some tact, as pressing too hard can cause them to break apart.

One interesting portion of the upper section, though, was the suspended secondary mirror, which clicks into to the panels as they are attached. These panels also lock into one another in a very satisfying way. Additionally, there's a single removable panel here that allows you to peek inside at some more of the components.

At the very end of the upper shaft is the aperture door, which features a hinge that allows you to open or close it, just like on the real Hubble Telescope.

Once the two halves of the Hubble's body are put together, all that's left is the finishing touches. This includes attaching the two communication antennas, which can be folded down or extended and rotated in any orientation, as well as building the two large solar arrays.

Thankfully, the solar arrays aren't giant stickers, as I feared when I saw the initial photographs of this set. Instead, they are thin plastic sheets with the printed solar panels on one side, and shiny silver on the back. Once attached to the telescope's body, they can be easily articulated to face any direction.

The entire time I was putting this set together, I kept wondering just how it was going to rest on the stand. It turns out, there's a small hole in the center of the body that the stand inserts into. But, because this set is a bit top-heavy, it can be slightly wobbly when on the stand when it's not stationary.

Overall, the finished product looks great on display. LEGO did an excellent job recreating the Hubble Space Telescope's iconic design and this set is a must for space enthusiasts.

LEGO Hubble Space Telescope, Set #11382, retails for $139.99 and is composed of 1,252 pieces. It is available to purchase from Amazon and the LEGO Store .

articles.title: WoW Forever Beta Extended to Friday, Name Reservations Go Live Tuesday
articles.summary: The World of Warcraft Forever beta has been incredibly popular, but just like any other beta, it has to come to an end as the full launch approaches. But Blizzard has extended the beta by a couple of days.
articles.body:
The World of Warcraft Forever beta has been incredibly popular, but just like any other, it has to come to an end as the full launch approaches. Thankfully, Blizzard has extended the beta by a couple of days.

WoW Forever's beta was supposed to end yesterday, October 20, but Blizzard announced on X/Twitter that it would be extending the experience by three days. Now the beta will end on October 23 at 10am PT / 1pm ET. After it ends, Blizzard will open name reservations on October 27, which will let you reserve names for three different characters – just make sure they don't break the rules.

It's easy to forget that WoW Forever isn't just out already. Since the beta went live in September, people have been playing it constantly, and just among people playing the beta, there have already been a million characters made. Blizzard devs have even come out and said they were surprised by how many people flocked to the temporary test version of the Classic+ game mode.

Once the full game comes out on November 4, all you'll need to play WoW: Forever is an active subscription or a friend code (though that will just be temporary), so it'll likely be even more popular.

Fans have loved how true the content in the beta so far has stayed to the spirit of the early days of World of Warcraft. Blizzard has made it a point to avoid adding some modern quality-of-life improvements like shared tagging in order to maintain that classic feel. But, rather than strictly avoiding adding anything that was added after WoW's expansions started coming out, Blizzard has included content like the beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' quest that takes place in Mulgore.

There have been controversies, too, of course – it wouldn't be WoW without them. Blizzard has had to crack down hard on gold selling , and the company has also been strict with character names . We've even seen people griefing other players by putting down campfires where new players spawn so they die before the intro cinematic finishes.

If you haven't had a chance to dive into the beta yet, you still have a couple days to do so. But keep in mind that any progress you make will be deleted when the game launches in a couple of weeks.

articles.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming’s pay-as-you-go option starts at $3.99 for 10 hours
articles.summary: Microsoft is opening up Xbox Cloud Gaming to anyone in November.
articles.body: Microsoft announced last month that it will let anyone access Xbox Cloud Gaming in November, without the need to subscribe to Xbox Game Pass. The new pay-as-you-go model will require players to purchase bundles of cloud hours, and now Microsoft is revealing today that bundles will start at $3.99 for 10 hours of cloud playtime. Xbox Insiders who don’t have a Game Pass subscription will be able to start purchasing cloud playtime today, ahead of a broader rollout next month. Insiders can access “introductory” launch pricing bundles: * 10 hours for $3.99 * 25 hours for $7.99 * 50 hours for $11.99 All of these cloud hours will include ad-free cloud gaming, shorter wait times, and higher-quality streaming. These aren’t monthly bundles of hours either, so once you purchased a pack it remains available until the hours are used. The pay-as-you-go Xbox Cloud Gaming option arrives just in time for Grand Theft Auto VI. I reported earlier this month that Microsoft has secured Grand Theft Auto VI streaming rights, but it’s not yet clear if this will be limited to just Xbox consoles. Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball revealed on X that Microsoft won’t be streaming Grand Theft Auto VI to PCs, suggesting that the web browsers and apps that can usually access Xbox Cloud Gaming will not be able to stream Grand Theft Auto VI. Microsoft also continues to test free, ad-supported cloud gaming for Xbox Insiders, offering up another way to stream games without Game Pass. The free streaming sessions are limited to games you already own, and sessions are capped at one hour.

The change means those who use cloud gaming most via Game Pass will end up having to pay more, although Microsoft said this impacts 4% of Game Pass subscribers.

Cloud gaming has become a focus as the RAMpocalypse makes console gaming increasingly expensive. Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently predicted the video game industry will be in “commercial streaming mode” within three years — but for video game streaming to matter, it would have to run GTA 6 just as well as consoles do.

During an investor focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, Zelnick was asked for his thoughts on the video game industry as it buckles under the pressure of skyrocketing chip costs, which have forced Sony and Microsoft to raise the price of their consoles and potentially delay the launches of the PlayStation 6 and the next-gen Xbox, codenamed Project Helix.

Zelnick admitted the rising cost of hardware “is not a good thing,” because cheaper hardware means more hardware in people’s hands, which is what software companies desire. But he suggested the advent of video game streaming would go a long way to tackling this problem.

Both Sony and Microsoft are predicted to lean heavily on streaming in the coming years as they contend with the RAMpocalypse. “I just don't have any insight as to what the console manufacturers have planned, but it wouldn't at all surprise me if part of what they plan is streaming,” Zelnick offered.

Just this week, it was reported that the next-gen Xbox may cost as much as $1,800 , with a new handheld rumored for next year. New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. She added that the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.

The current PS5 and Xbox Series X and S generation of consoles have seen price increases rather than cost savings. Sony itself raised the price of PS5 consoles back in March , blaming “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.” Nintendo has also not been immune, and recently acknowledged it would up the price of Switch 2, just over a year after its arrival. And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped , instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

articles.title: Glee Reboot Is Officially a Go at Disney+ and Hulu, and Gleeks Have Plenty of Thoughts
articles.summary: Disney+ and Hulu have officially picked up a series order of Ryan Murphy’s Glee reboot.
articles.body:
Disney+ and Hulu have officially picked up a series order of Ryan Murphy’s Glee reboot.

Murphy first revealed the possibility of a revival in July when he expressed his continued love for the musical series during an interview with People . By September, Murphy announced a finished script, alongside confirmation that he’s already spoken to “about 10 or so” original cast members about returning. While the series order announcement didn't initially reveal any casting news, original cast members like Lea Michele and Heather Morris have since confirmed their involvement.

Gleeks are reacting strongly to the news: “This is the best worst day of my life,” commented one fan. “This is gonna be so bad! I’m so happy and can’t wait,” said another.

Currently gleeking out! — GLEE (@gleeofficial) October 21, 2026

Why the complicated feelings? Well, in the words of one dedicated Gleek account , “No one is more against this reboot than Gleeks because we all remember its excruciating devolution into insanity.”

While the early seasons of Glee were as critically acclaimed as they were popular, later seasons relied on shock plot lines while struggling to balance a rotating cast of characters. Murphy himself has developed quite the reputation for occasional tone deafness, most recently on display in the true crime Netflix series Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story , with an imagined ending that treats the serial killer series as some kind of MCU multiverse .

Fans’ primary concern, however? Whether we'll see a full reunion of the original cast. One fan argues that “a Glee revival with no cast announced is just a really expensive school choir.”

Some fans have particularly strong opinions on who exactly from the original cast is worth bringing back: “They need to go to Jane Lynch and offer her 1 billion dollars to return because thats the only way this is going to have a chance to work.” Lynch, who played the sardonic cheerleading coach Sue Sylvester, won an Emmy for the role in 2010.

The overwhelming majority of Gleeks have gathered in the comment sections of the announcement to pay tribute to the original cast members, arguing against bringing the series back without them. Per one fan , “Glee without Naya is like earth without water.” Rivera, who played fan-favorite Cheerio Santana Lopez, passed away in a tragic accident in 2020.

Fans also express concern over the reboot potentially “re-evaluating” some of the canon arcs from the original show, particularly the show’s groundbreaking queer relationships. “Don’t touch Brittana,” and “Don’t touch Klaine” are common refrains in the replies.

Still, some fans have a lot to gain from the show’s return. Popular X gimmick account Terri Schuester Updates , which has been consistently active since the show’s cancellation, was quick to recognize what this update means for their own career: “Wait, does this mean I might finally have some actual Terri Schuester updates?”

Other fans are already theorizing about what music will make its way into the reboot, pitching recent breakout popstars like Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan. One particularly popular post jokingly takes a more simplistic stance on the reboot as a whole: “We’re about to get soooo many more songs to say 'they sang this on Glee' to, and that’s really what life is all about.”

Will that be enough reason for fans to tune into the reboot on Disney+? We’ll have to wait and see.

articles.title: Meet Valkyrie, Milwaukee's bald eagle starring in World Series pregame
articles.summary: Valkyrie the bald eagle has been at playoff games before. She's cool under pressure and is raising awareness for the nature conservation.
articles.body:
Before the Brewers take the field for Game 1 of the World Series, another Milwaukee star will take center stage – a bald eagle named Valkyrie.

Valkyrie is a 15-year-old bald eagle at Milwaukee's Schlitz Audubon Nature Center who will be presented during the national anthem before Game 1 of the World Series, happening at 7 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23 .

This won't be Valkyrie's first start either. She was also there for Game 1 of both the National League Division Series and the National League Championship Series.

Valkyrie won't fly around during the anthem, but will instead stay with her handler. But don't worry – she doesn't shy away from a big moment. Valkyrie has been trained to handle loud crowd noises and moving flags to help her stay calm amid the World Series chaos.

Lindsay Focht , raptor program director for the Schlitz Audubon Nature Center, said Valkyrie isn't able to live in the wild. She hatched in the wild, but at 6 months old she was fed by humans. She "made the association that people are great," Focht said, and was eventually scooped up by the nature center.

Focht said this is the second year the bald eagle has been at Brewers' games and it has been wonderful for visibility. There has been an uptick in interest in the program with more people asking to book birds.

The program's goal is to educate people. They might show up in classrooms, libraries or even the World Series. Focht said if there's any takeaway people should have, it should be to learn more and enjoy nature.

"Come to one of our free raptor programs and just enjoy what nature has to offer," she said.

Before the 2026 Milwaukee Brewers, there were the 1982 Milwaukee Brewers. That had been the last team in franchise history to make a World Series. The '82 Brewers were part of the American League at the time and won the AL East with a 95-67-1 record. The team known as Harvey's Wallbangers, a nod to their manager Harvey Kuenn, a West Allis native, then beat the California Angels in a best-of-five American League Championship Series. They rallied to win the final three games of the series to win the AL pennant after losing the first two games on the road. While the World Series didn't end with a championship - the Brewers lost in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals - the cast of characters is remembered and beloved to this day in Milwaukee. articles.title: Xbox mandates a four-day return to office
articles.summary: Xbox employees close to Microsoft’s Redmond headquarters will need to come into the office more starting in February.
articles.body: Microsoft asked its employees to return to the office three days per week last year, and it’s now upping this requirement to four days a week for most Xbox employees. An internal memo, seen by The Verge, describes the change as a “need to create more opportunities for people to work together” after feedback from Xbox employees. “Starting February 1st, 2027, Xbox employees in Puget Sound who live within 50 commuting miles of Studio D are required to work from the office a minimum of four days a week,” says Jacinda Chislum Pearson, Xbox chief people officer, in the internal memo. “We have thousands of Xbox employees within commuting distance of Redmond. Taking advantage of that proximity and working together in person makes it easier to review work, resolve issues, and make decisions without the burden of scheduling another meeting.” The change to four days in the office will only apply to those close to Microsoft’s corporate campus in Redmond, Washington, and Pearson’s memo appears to suggest that “established in-office practices” for Xbox studios will remain unchanged. Microsoft has had exemptions to its return to office rules for certain roles, and Xbox employees with existing exemptions will need to resubmit them again. The return to office changes come just a day after a report suggested Microsoft was planning to announce further Xbox layoffs this month, and in November and January. Microsoft announced in July that it was planning to eliminate around 20 percent of Xbox jobs by the end of its financial year at the end of June 2027. Xbox is also positioning its updated return to office policy as one that “should be worth the investment” of taking the time to commute into the office, especially for those 40-50 miles away. “Leaders should be present, and coming into the office should not mean spending the same day on Teams calls from a different building,” says Pearson. “Time well spent means reviewing work, solving problems, and playing games together, strengthening our path to becoming one Xbox.”

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077’s update for Edgerunners 2 brings mods to PS5, Switch 2, and Xbox
articles.summary: Cyberpunk 2077’s 2.5 update starts rolling out on October 22nd, with new content tied to Edgerunners season two and access to player-created mods on consoles.
articles.body: Cyberpunk 2077 is getting a big new 2.5 update that, among other features, brings cross-platform mod support to consoles and content inspired by the new season of the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime on Netflix. There’s a lot to unpack in the full patch notes. The Edgerunners-specific content includes a new side quest, a gear set based on the character Weak Kingsley, and a new radio station that plays Cyberpunk: Edgerunners music. [Media: Even if you haven’t seen the show, the update also adds a Double Trouble perk option that allows dual-wielding of pistols and revolvers, plus a Richard Night-guided tour of the city side quest, and access to a selection of player-created mods via the in-game menu. > Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2. The new mod support extends to the currently supported consoles too, and CDPR says that more mods will become available over time. The notes don’t say which mods will be available at first, but it could extend the lifespan of a game that’s already nearly six years clear of its initially-troubled launch, even without the missing multiplayer mode. Other tweaks include grouped saves that are sorted by playthrough, DLSS 4.5 support and glasses-free 3D effects, and an FOV slider for console players who want to see more (or less). The update launches on October 22nd on PC, Mac, PS5, and Xbox Series X / S, while it’s coming to Nintendo Switch 2 and the Mac App Store in the “days to follow,” according to CD Projekt Red’s patch notes.

articles.title: Poison Ivy Show in Early Development with Penguin Showrunner in Talks to Produce
articles.summary: Deadline has confirmed that DC Comics’ Poison Ivy is in the early stages of getting her own live-action TV show, and one of the minds that brought us the critically-acclaimed Penguin series is in discussions to produce it.
articles.body:
Deadline has confirmed that DC Comics’ Poison Ivy is in the early stages of getting her own live-action TV show, and one of the minds that brought us the critically acclaimed Penguin series is in discussions to produce it.

However, the outlet’s sources state that this show won’t be part of Matt Reeves’ Batman universe, so don’t get your hopes up for the chance of seeing Colin Farrell’s Penguin or Battinson sharing the screen with Dr. Isley.

Lauren LeFranc, showrunner and executive producer on HBO’s The Penguin series, is currently in talks to produce the Poison Ivy show. If it gets picked up, it’ll also go to HBO for streaming, but it’s still very early days for the project.

The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel

Right now, there are no writers attached to the series, and no cast has been revealed, either. It’s anyone’s guess as to who will get the leading role (Uma Thurman is a hard act to follow), but there’s plenty of freedom to be had, given that Poison Ivy is a character that hasn’t yet been represented in newer DC projects.

Thus far, she hasn’t shown up in James Gunn’s DC cinematic universe, and there’s been no word on the character’s involvement in the next Batman film . It’s worth noting that Scarlett Johansson is confirmed as part of the movie’s cast, sparking no end of fan theories as to who she’ll be portraying. While rumors suggest she's playing Harvey Dent's wife, Gilda Dent, many fan theories are hoping against hope that she'll be Poison Ivy. We have to admit that she would be a perfect fit for the DC anti-hero/villainess, and it would be a smashing debut for the actress in the DCU, following Black Widow’s exit from the MCU in Avengers: Endgame .

Poison Ivy’s most prominent appearance as of late has been in DC Studios’ animated Harley Quinn show , where her romance with her fellow villain takes center stage. It’d be exciting to see if this relationship is also included in the live-action series, and who will be cast as Harley Quinn if so. (Margot Robbie is most likely off the table with the new DCU reboot. Gunn himself has been rather coy about the whole thing, saying in August 2025 that Robbie's potential future in the DCU "will be revealed down the line." )

While they wait, fans can look forward to Clayface , which hits theaters on October 23. IGN’s Jim Vejvoda scored the film a 7 out of 10 , saying it’s “a fun body horror romp that realizes its nasty potential in its final act after a slow-burn set-up.”
